comparison: Retained published v0.34 and installed v0.35; optionally retain the initial v0.35 as a third graph when optimizing. Prior runtime and unrelated host source must match byte-for-byte.
order: Rotate the first graph each trial, including warmup. One sequential benchmark process, no competing verification/build jobs.
memoryMethod: Use native scheduling, release warning flashes, then compare twice-forced-GC retained heap with and without the pending queue while the same World remains alive. Two amplified sizes and seven rotating paired samples. Includes queue array, captured positions and scaled payloads; excludes released warnings. Not allocation volume, normal occupancy, peak memory or per-World constructor cost.
receipt: Every timed sample must produce identical full canonical observations across graphs and trials. Hash queue payloads, actor combat/proc state, texts and flashes; record random draws, damage/healing changes, frame/cast counts and queue occupancy. Assert that each intended path actually ran.
timing: Setup, forced GC, observation serialization and equality checks are outside timing. Native scheduling/contact/frame loops, delivery, host callback work, RNG count and queue-occupancy observation are included. Prebuilt delivery waves replace the inactive queue between native drains to isolate delivery cost.
reporting: Keep every sample, batch median, p95 and per-call/per-frame interpretation. Report both independent runs, including regressions and noise; do not select the best trial or extrapolate desktop Node results to Steam Deck/mobile, renderer FPS or general game performance.
optimization: Only change measured costs with retained initial controls and unchanged behavioral/cancellation evidence. No database, heap, spatial-index or pooling change without a demonstrated workload advantage and valid ownership/order semantics.
